items.q: Sandblaster with upper lobe conglomerate fibrosis and eggshell nodes most likely suffers which pneumoconiosis complicated by TB risk?
items.exp: Silica exposure in sandblasting and stone work causes upper lobe progressive massive fibrosis with eggshell hilar calcification and macrophage impairment reactivating tuberculosis needing lifelong vigilance.
r: Incorrect. Asbestos favours lower lobes and pleura.
Correct. Eggshell massive fibrosis means silicosis.
Incorrect. Beryllium granulomas mimic sarcoid without eggshell pattern.
Incorrect. Iron siderosis is relatively benign welder disease.
items.kp: Sand plus eggshell plus upper scars equals silicosis. Watch TB.

items.q: Calcified pleural plaques in a retired shipyard insulator indicate what significance?
o: Asbestos exposure marker, usually asymptomatic without fibrosis proof
items.exp: Pleural plaques are hyaline collagen receipts of asbestos exposure, typically asymptomatic and not premalignant themselves, while asbestosis requires parenchymal fibrosis and mesothelioma needs tumour diagnosis separately.
r: Incorrect. Plaques are benign exposure markers, not tumours.
Correct. Plaques receipt exposure without proving disease.
Incorrect. TB pleurisy scars differently without this exposure pattern.
Incorrect. Plaques are not universal ageing findings.
items.kp: Plaques prove exposure, not cancer. Fibrosis and tumour need own proof.

items.q: Progressive massive fibrosis in coal miners is distinguished from simple pneumoconiosis how?
o: Large conglomerate opacities over 1 cm with disabling fibrosis, cavitation risk
items.exp: Progressive massive fibrosis forms large conglomerate fibrotic masses (often upper posterior) causing restriction, pulmonary hypertension and sometimes cavitation, unlike simple macular disease with preserved function. It may advance after exposure ceases.
r: Incorrect. That describes simple coal disease.
Correct. Conglomerates disabling lungs mean massive fibrosis.
Incorrect. Mesothelioma belongs to asbestos exposure.
Incorrect. Massive fibrosis can progress despite removal.
items.kp: Coal disease disables only when masses conglomerate.

items.q: Farmer develops fever, cough and breathlessness six hours after handling mouldy hay, resolving in days. Likely diagnosis?
items.exp: Acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis is immune alveolitis to thermophilic actinomycetes in mouldy hay causing flu like pulmonary episodes four to eight hours post exposure, with lavage lymphocytosis and avoidance curative.
r: Incorrect. Silicosis is chronic fibrotic over years.
Correct. Timed post hay episodes mean farmer lung.
Incorrect. Asbestosis never flares episodically like this.
Incorrect. Massive fibrosis is fixed disabling disease.
items.kp: Hours after antigen, sick lungs: hypersensitivity pneumonitis.

items.q: Caplan syndrome combines pneumoconiosis with which systemic disease producing necrobiotic lung nodules?
items.exp: Caplan described rheumatoid pneumoconiosis (coal or silica) with rapidly erupting necrobiotic nodules resembling rheumatoid nodules cavitating in lungs, in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and dust exposure.
r: Incorrect. Lupus pleurises without Caplan nodules.
Correct. Rheumatoid plus dust equals Caplan syndrome.
Incorrect. Sarcoid granulomas are non necrobiotic differently distributed.
Incorrect. Scleroderma fibroses bases without eruptive nodules.
items.kp: Rheumatoid joints plus dusty lungs plus nodules: Caplan.

items.q: Beryllium exposure in aerospace workers causes lung disease mimicking which condition granulomatously?
o: Sarcoidosis (chronic beryllium disease, sensitisation tested by lymphocyte proliferation)
items.exp: Chronic beryllium disease is cell mediated granulomatous lung disease indistinguishable from sarcoidosis clinically, separated by exposure history and beryllium lymphocyte proliferation testing.
r: Incorrect. Asbestos fibroses lower lobes with pleural disease.
Correct. Beryllium mimics sarcoid granulomas.
Incorrect. Eggshell fibrosis belongs to silica.
Incorrect. Farmer lung is episodic immune alveolitis.
items.kp: Sarcoid lookalike with metal exposure: test beryllium sensitisation.

items.q: Byssinosis (Monday chest tightness) in textile workers is caused by inhaling what?
o: Cotton dust endotoxin causing reversible weekly airflow obstruction
items.exp: Byssinosis is cotton (and flax, hemp) dust endotoxin airway disease worst on returning after weekends (Monday fever and tightness), improving through the week, distinct from chronic fibrotic pneumoconioses.
r: Incorrect. Stone silica fibroses upper lobes chronically.
Correct. Cotton dust causes Monday byssinosis.
Incorrect. Asbestos causes lower fibrosis and pleural disease.
Incorrect. Coal macules do not cycle weekly like this.
items.kp: Monday tight chest in mill workers equals byssinosis.

items.q: Ferruginous (asbestos) bodies in lung tissue prove what precisely?
o: Mesothelioma causation in that patient alone
Asbestos fibre inhalation exposure (coated fibres), not by themselves clinical asbestosis disease
items.exp: Asbestos bodies are inhaled fibres coated with iron protein proving exposure burden, found in exposed healthy lungs too; asbestosis diagnosis additionally requires interstitial fibrosis pattern and exposure dose latency context.
r: Incorrect. Causation needs disease pattern beyond bodies.
Correct. Bodies receipt exposure, disease needs fibrosis.
Incorrect. Silica particles are not ferruginous coated fibres.
Incorrect. TB needs microbiological or granuloma evidence.
items.kp: Bodies prove breathing fibres, not suffering disease.

items.q: Acute silicoproteinosis after intense sandblasting resembles which alveolar filling disease pathologically?
o: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAS positive lipoprotein alveolar filling)
items.exp: Massive acute silica inhalation overwhelms macrophages filling alveoli with surfactant like PAS positive material (silicoproteinosis) causing rapid respiratory failure, distinct from chronic nodular silicosis timeline.
r: Incorrect. Oedema is cardiac hydrostatic pink froth different context.
Correct. Alveolar proteinosis pattern after massive silica.
Incorrect. Haemorrhage fills with blood and haemosiderin.
Incorrect. Pneumocystis foamy exudate infects immunosuppressed hosts.
items.kp: Massive silica in months floods alveoli like proteinosis.

items.q: Bagassosis, bird fancier lung and maple bark disease share which mechanism family?
items.exp: These are hypersensitivity pneumonitides to organic antigens (sugarcane mould, avian proteins, maple bark fungi) causing immune granulomatous alveolitis acute to chronic, treated by antigen avoidance.
r: Incorrect. No inorganic fibre drives these diseases.
Correct. Organic antigen immune alveolitis unites them.
Incorrect. Carcinogenesis is asbestos fibre territory.
Incorrect. Metals cause silicosis like or beryllium patterns.
items.kp: Named occupation lungs with antigens equal hypersensitivity family.
